keeps it faint. It is anchored to the text's own column (`max-w-3xl`, at the parent's left edge),
never the viewport, and clipped to it, so nothing scrolls sideways on a phone. It is
`aria-hidden`, and the text sits above it. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` it stands still.
Pure markup and one inline stylesheet: it works rendered on the server with no script.
One per page, on a landing page; every other page opens with a `PageHeader`.

props.name: children
props.description: What follows the title: a `Lead`, and the page's first actions if it has any.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: overline
props.description: The small label above the title, set in the monospace face.

props.name: title
props.description: The page's `h1`, at display size.

Icon.name: Icon
Icon.description:
One inline icon, sized to a fixed box (sm 14px, md 16px, lg 20px, `feature` 32px) and drawn in
`currentColor`, so it takes the text colour around it unless a `tone` says otherwise. `name`
picks one of the library's own icons, all drawn on one grid with one stroke: feature ideas
(`diff`, `baseline`, `review`, `ci`, `self-host`, `privacy`, `capture`, `branch`, `theme`,
`speed`, `search`) and UI glyphs (`chevron-right`, `chevron-down`, `close`, `external-link`,
`settings`, `bell`, `check`, `plus`, `more`) and the ideas the docs sections stand for (`grid`, `window`,
`type`, `card`, `pointer`, `field`, `table`, `compass`, `page`, `briefcase`);
without a name, a bare `<svg>` child fills the box. It is decorative (`aria-hidden`) by
default; a `label` makes it an image with that name, for an icon that carries meaning no text
beside it says.

props.name: children
props.description: The `<svg>`, drawn in `currentColor`; it fills the box.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the icon (`role="img"`). Without one the icon is hidden from assistive tech.

props.name: name
props.description: One of the library's icons, named for the idea it stands for.

props.name: size
props.description: The box: sm 14px, md 16px (the default), lg 20px, `feature` 32px for an icon that stands for an idea on its own (a feature card).

props.name: tone
props.description: A text tone. Left out, the icon takes the colour of the text around it.

IconButton.name: IconButton
IconButton.description:
A square button holding one icon from the `Icon` set (`icon`). `label` is its accessible name
and tooltip. `variant="ghost"` drops the border for a quiet action in a row or a toolbar; `size`
matches the height of a `Button` of the same size (`sm` 26px, `md` 38px, `lg` 46px) and with no
`size` it takes its container's; `tone="danger"` is red, for delete and clear; `count` pins a
red count to the corner; `disabledReason` blocks it and shows why. Defaults to `type="button"`. `href` makes it a link instead (the app's
router link through `LinkProvider` for an in-app path, else a plain `<a>`; `external` opens a
new tab), with the same look.

props.name: count
props.description: A red count on the top-right corner, for unread alerts. Not shown at 0; the name carries it for a screen reader, "Alerts, 3".

props.name: disabledReason
props.description:
Why the button cannot be pressed: it dims and is blocked (`aria-disabled`; a click, Enter and
Space do nothing) while it stays in the tab order, and the reason is its tooltip on hover,
keyboard focus and a tap, read out as its description. The name stays `label`.

props.name: external
props.description: Opens in a new tab: adds `target="_blank"` and `rel="noreferrer"`.

props.name: href
props.description: Makes the button a link to this URL; an in-app path goes through the app's `LinkProvider`.

props.name: icon
props.description: The one icon it holds, from the `Icon` set, at the button's size.

props.name: label
props.description: The button's accessible name and its tooltip, shown on hover and on keyboard focus.

props.name: size
props.description:
The button's height, matching a `Button` or `Input` of the same size. Left out, it takes the
size of the `Card`, `ListRow` or `Table` it sits in, else `md`.

props.name: tone
props.description: `danger` is red, for delete and clear.

props.name: variant
props.description: `outline` has a border; `ghost` has none, until the hover fill.

Image.name: Image
Image.description:
A picture in a fixed shape: `aspect` reserves the space before it loads, so the page does not
jump, and `fit` crops it to the shape or shows all of it. The corners are rounded and the frame
has a hairline. If the picture is missing or fails to load, a same-sized placeholder with a
picture mark stands in, still named by `alt`. `framed` mats a code or a logo in white. A user's photo is an `Avatar`; a clickable
thumbnail with a label is a `MediaTile`. While `loading` with no `src` yet it is a bone of the same
shape, not the placeholder, which means there is no picture.

props.name: alt
props.description: What the picture shows. An empty string marks it as decoration, hidden from a screen reader.

props.name: aspect
fit
props.description:
`cover` fills the shape and crops what overflows; `contain` shows the whole picture, with the
rest of the shape left empty (a QR code, a logo).

props.name: framed
props.description:
Sets the picture on a white mat with padding, always white, in every theme: a QR code is
scanned off a dark page. It shows the whole picture, as `fit="contain"`, whatever `fit` says.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: src
props.description:
The picture, a local path or a data URL. It is never loaded for you: this is the app's own
image. Left out, or if it fails to load, the picture is replaced by a placeholder.

props.name: width
props.description: `sm` 96px, `md` 160px and `lg` 256px set the width, capped at the parent's; `full` fills the parent.

InlineEdit.name: InlineEdit
InlineEdit.description:
A value that opens an editor in place, as a part inside a `TableCell` that holds more than the
value (an edit trigger in a column cell with other content, say). It shows `children` as a button with a dotted underline; a click, Enter
or Space swaps it for `renderEditor(close)` and moves the focus into the editor. The part keeps
its own open state. The editor calls `close` when it has saved, and Esc closes it: both put the
focus back on the value. A press outside it or Tab out of it closes it too and leaves the focus
where it went, so the editor saves its value on its own change or submit, never on a close. Put
the control in the part itself, not in a popover of its own, which counts as outside. It takes
the alignment of the cell around it. It is a block that bleeds half a rem into the padding of
the cell it sits in, so it belongs inside a `TableCell`; a cell that holds only the value is a
`TableEditCell`. `data-*` and `aria-*` go on the button, and on the editor's group while open.

props.name: children
props.description: The value, shown while closed.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: What the button does, for a screen reader, heard after the value: "Edit category". It also names the editor.

props.name: renderEditor
props.description: The control that edits the value, drawn while open. `close` shuts it and returns the focus to the value.

Input.name: Input
Input.description:
A text input. `icon` names a leading icon inside the field (`icon="search"`). `prefix` puts
short text inside the border before the value, such as a currency symbol; it is for a plain
field, not with an `icon` or `type="search"`. `numeric` is a field for a figure: an amount
(`<Input prefix="R" numeric />`) or a count (`numeric inputMode="numeric"`). It right-aligns the
value in tabular figures and brings up the phone's number keypad (`inputMode="decimal"` unless
you pass your own), and stays a text field, so "1 250" is kept as typed; never use
`type="number"` for a figure a person types. `type="search"` drops the browser's own search look and shows a clear button at the
trailing edge while the field has a value, named by `clearLabel`. The `ref` reaches the `<input>`.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: The name of a `type="search"` field's clear button, for an app in another language.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the field; say why in its `Field` hint.

props.name: icon
props.description: A leading icon inside the field, by name (`search`). Not with `prefix`.

props.name: name
props.description: The key the value posts under in a form.

props.name: numeric
props.description:
A field for a figure (an amount, a count): the value right-aligned in tabular figures, and
`inputMode="decimal"` unless you pass your own (`numeric` for a whole number). It stays a
text field, so the value is kept as typed; parsing it is yours. Ignored on `type="search"`.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: A hint shown while the field is empty; never the label.

props.name: prefix
props.description: Short text inside the border before the value (a currency symbol). For a plain field: not with `icon` or `type="search"`.

props.name: ref
props.description: The `<input>` itself, for focus control.

props.name: required
props.description: The form will not submit while the field is empty.

props.name: size
type
props.description: The kind of value: `"text"`, `"email"`, `"search"`, `"password"` and the rest.

props.name: width
props.description: `full` (default) fills the parent; `fill` grows to fill the room left in a row beside other items (it can shrink to nothing, so buttons stay on the line); `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg` are fixed; `auto` adds no width class, so the control is as wide as the browser makes it.

Kbd.name: Kbd
Kbd.description: A keyboard key. Its border takes the surrounding text colour, so it reads on a filled button and on plain text.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

KeyValue.name: KeyValue
KeyValue.description:
One row of a KeyValueList: a label on the left, a tabular value on the right (or beside it, in an
`align="start"` list). `total` makes it the sum row: a rule above, strong text. `tone` colours the
value, on any row: a total that does not reconcile is `total tone="warn"`. While `loading`, a
label or value not here yet is a bone.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The term, on the left.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: tone
props.description: The meaning of the value, in the colours of a `Table` cell's `tone` (`TextTone`; `neutral`, the default, is the list's ink); the label keeps its ink. Colour alone does not say it, so the value or the label says it too: a sign, a word.

props.name: total
props.description: The sum the rows above add up to: a firm rule above it and the label and value in strong ink.

KeyValueList.name: KeyValueList
KeyValueList.description:
A definition list of label/value rows. By default each label is on the left and its value
right-aligned. `align="start"` puts every value left-aligned in one column beside the labels,
which are sized to the widest. While `loading` with no rows it draws three rows of bones.

props.name: align
props.description: `end` right-aligns each value; `start` puts every value left-aligned in one column beside the labels, sized to the widest.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

Lead.name: Lead
Lead.description: The supporting sentence under a `Display`. `p`, text-lg/7 normal, secondary.

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render (each role has a semantic default); the other props follow it.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

Legend.name: Legend
Legend.description:
A key to the colours of a chart or a row stripe: a swatch in the `VizTone` colour (a filled
dot, or a dashed ring with `swatch="dashed"`), its `label` and an optional `detail` after it. Colour alone does not say it, so the label is always drawn.
`StackedBar legend` draws one under the bar from its segments.
While `loading` with no `items` it draws three entries of bones.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: items
props.description: One entry per colour: its `label`, its `tone`, an optional `swatch` and `detail` (a count, a share).

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

Lightbox.name: Lightbox
Lightbox.description:
A full-screen photo or video viewer on the browser's own `<dialog>`: it is opened with
`showModal()` on mount, so render it only while it is open. The page behind goes inert, Esc
closes it and focus stays inside; a click on the scrim around the media and its text closes it
too. The scrim stays near-black with light text in every theme. `onPrevious` and `onNext` add
step buttons and the arrow keys.

props.name: caption
props.description: Muted text on the scrim under the media.

props.name: children
props.description: The media: one `` or `

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: The close button's name, for an app in another language.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The viewer's accessible name, e.g. "Photo from Anna".

props.name: meta
props.description: A muted line under the title, e.g. when.

props.name: nextLabel
props.description: The next button's name.

props.name: onClose
props.description: Called when the viewer closes: Esc, a click on the scrim or the close button.

props.name: onNext
props.description: Shows a next button and binds ArrowRight. Leave it out at the last item.

props.name: onPrevious
props.description: Shows a previous button and binds ArrowLeft. Leave it out at the first item.

props.name: previousLabel
props.description: The previous button's name.

props.name: title
props.description: A line on the scrim above the media, e.g. who posted it.

LinkProvider.name: LinkProvider
LinkProvider.description:
Names the app's router link once, so every part that links (`Button`, `IconButton`, `TextLink`,
`Pill`, `Card`, `ListRow`, `Breadcrumbs`, `Tabs`, `SegmentedControl`, `AppShellBrand`,
`SiteSearch`, `MediaTile`, `Avatar` and the status pages) takes a plain `href` and draws an in-app
one (a path from the root, `/quotes?page=2#top`) through the router. It renders no element.

- TanStack Router: `createRouter({ routeTree, InnerWrap: ({ children }) => <LinkProvider link={(p) => <Link to="." {...p} />}>{children}</LinkProvider> })`,
  which also reaches the router's not-found and error components. A registered router's `Link`
  requires `to`; `to="."` satisfies it, and the `href` wins.
- React Router: `<LinkProvider link={({ href, ...p }) => <Link to={href} {...p} />}>` inside the router.
- Astro, or no router: no provider; every link is a plain `<a>`.

An `external` link, a full URL (`https:`, `mailto:`, `tel:`), a `//` URL, a `#hash` or a relative
path never reaches the adapter: the library draws those as a plain `<a>`.

`home` is where every status page's "Back to home" goes, `/` by default: the one place an app
says it, never a page. A full URL (a home on another site) is a plain `<a>` in the same tab. A
provider inside another keeps what it does not set, so `<LinkProvider home="/app">` within the
router's provider still draws through the router's link.

props.name: home
props.description: Where the status pages' "Back to home" goes: an in-app path or a full URL.

props.name: link
props.description: The app's router link, handed `LinkAdapterProps`. Left out, links are plain `<a>` (or the outer provider's).

ListLayout.name: ListLayout
ListLayout.description: A list page: header, an optional `filters` slot, then the list, or `empty` when there are no children. While `loading` it owns the wait and passes it to everything inside, the header too. With no children yet it draws a card of row bones, never `empty`.

props.name: actions
props.description: Right of the title on `sm` and up, below it on a phone.

props.name: breadcrumbs
props.description: A `Breadcrumbs` above the title.

props.name: description
props.description: The lede under the title: a `Lead`, so it outranks the body text after it.

props.name: empty
props.description: Shown in place of `children` when there are none (no rows, an empty array, `null`): an `EmptyState`.

props.name: filters
props.description: A row between the header and the list, e.g. a `Fieldset` of chips or an `Input type="search"`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: tabs
props.description: A `Tabs` (or similar) under the title.

props.name: title
props.description: The page's `h1`.

ListRow.name: ListRow
ListRow.description:
A full-width row that runs `onClick` (or, with `href`, opens a link) with a hover
fill, a left-aligned label and `trailing` content at the far end. The row is a `<div>` with its
`<button>` or link stretched over it, so a tap anywhere on the row runs it; a `TextLink`,
`Button` or `Checkbox` in the row (in `trailing`, say a "View" link on a row that selects) sits
above it and is clickable on its own. A button row's button is named by the label alone. With `expanded` it is the header of a
collapsible section: `aria-expanded` and a chevron. Rows sit in a `Card flush`; `divided` draws
the line between them, on each row after the first.

`secondary` is a second, muted line under the label. `leading` is content before the label (`leadingWidth="thumbnail"` gives it a fixed picture width),
`selected` marks the row in view, `focused` the one the keyboard cursor is on and `highlighted` fills
the row a list follows (`onPointerEnter`, `onPointerLeave` and `onFocus` reach
every form; on a button or linked row the pointer handlers go on the row itself). The label is a
`<div>`, so it can hold block content (a name over a path). A row with no `href` and no
`onClick` is a plain `<div>` with no action of its own, for one that holds its own buttons:
`actions` follow `trailing`, and `revealOnHover` shows them only on hover or focus. Such a row
also takes a `panel`, content under the row that starts where the label does (a conversation
that opens under its chat); `divided` draws the line above the whole row, panel included, so a
list of them is `divided={index > 0}` on each. Inside a row a `Stack` is `xs` apart, and a `sm`
row makes the buttons in it `sm`. While `loading` an empty label is a bone, and what the row holds
waits with it.

props.name: actions
props.description: Buttons for this row, after `trailing`: `Button size="sm"`, `IconButton`.

props.name: disabledReason
props.description: Why the row cannot be pressed: it fades, `aria-disabled` and focusable, the reason its tooltip.

props.name: divided
props.description: A hairline above the row: set it on every row after the first.

props.name: expanded
props.description:
Makes the row a collapsible header: sets `aria-expanded` and shows a chevron that turns down
when open. The caller owns the state and the section; pass `aria-controls` to name it.

props.name: external
props.description: Opens in a new tab: adds `target="_blank"` and `rel="noreferrer"`.

props.name: focused
props.description:
Marks the row the keyboard cursor is on, for a list moved with the arrow keys or `j`/`k` while
focus stays on the list: the focus ring, drawn inside the row. It says nothing to a screen
reader (move real focus for that) and combines with `selected`.

props.name: highlighted
props.description:
Marks the row a list follows with the pointer and the keyboard alike (set it from
`onPointerEnter` and `onFocus`): a fill one step deeper than hover, so it shows on a white card
and on a tinted panel alike. On a static row it shows the fill without `revealOnHover`, and
shows `actions` that `revealOnHover` hides. `selected` wins.

props.name: href
props.description: Makes the row a link to this URL; an in-app path goes through the app's `LinkProvider`.

props.name: leading
props.description: Content before the label: an Avatar, a thumbnail, an icon.

props.name: leadingWidth
props.description: A fixed width for `leading`, for a thumbnail (an `` fills it), so the labels of rows with and without a picture still line up. Without it `leading` is as wide as its content.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: onClick
props.description: What the row does when pressed: it makes the row a button.

props.name: onPointerEnter
props.description: On the row, not its link or button, so a link or button in the row does not count as entering it.

props.name: onPointerLeave
props.description: On the row, not its link or button, so a link or button in the row does not count as leaving it.

props.name: panel
props.description:
Content under the row, lined up with the label rather than the row's edge (past `leading`): the
panel of a row that opens in place, such as a conversation under its chat. It sits inside the
row, so `divided`, the fill and `revealOnHover` cover it too. Only a row that is neither a
button nor a link takes it.

props.name: revealOnHover
props.description:
Hides `actions` until the row is hovered or something in it has focus, so a long list is not a
wall of buttons. A touch screen has no hover, so they are always shown there.

props.name: secondary
props.description: A second, muted line under the label (a date, a note), like `TableCell`'s `secondary`.

props.name: selected
props.description:
Marks the row in view, the one whose detail is open: an accent fill and `aria-current="true"`.
Set it on one row of a list.

props.name: size
props.description:
`sm` is dense padding, `lg` one step roomier than `md`. A `Button`, `IconButton` or `Pill` in a
`sm` row with no `size` of its own is `sm` too.

props.name: trailing
props.description: Content at the far end of the row: a value, a count, a Pill.

Maintenance.name: Maintenance
Maintenance.description:
The site is down on purpose and will be back: the page for planned downtime, such as an upgrade.
A failure is an `ErrorPage`, and no connection is `Offline`. It has no "Back to home": home is
the site that is down.

props.name: actions
props.description:
The page's own buttons, before "Back to home", which turns outline beside them. This is the one
way to a button worded differently; there is no label prop.

props.name: children
props.description: Replaces the default body copy.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: title
props.description: Replaces the default heading.

Markdown.name: Markdown
Markdown.description:
A small, safe Markdown renderer for short notes: `## ` and `### ` headings, `- ` or `* ` bullets,
`**bold**` and paragraphs. Text is rendered as React nodes, never as HTML. While `loading` with
no `md` yet it draws a paragraph of bones.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: md
props.description: The Markdown source; while `loading`, none yet is a paragraph of bones.

MediaTile.name: MediaTile
MediaTile.description:
A thumbnail tile: a picture in a fixed shape with an optional label on its bottom edge and a
caption under it. With `onClick` the whole tile is one button, which is how a grid or a
`ScrollStrip` of media opens each item in a `Lightbox`. The label sits on the same near-black
media scrim as the Lightbox, in every theme. The thumbnail is cropped to fill its shape, or with
`aspect="natural"` shown whole. With `href` the whole tile is one link instead. `onRemove` adds a
remove button for a tile that can be taken back out.
While `loading` with no `src` yet the picture is a bone of its shape.

props.name: alt
props.description: What the thumbnail shows; it is the tile's name, with `label`.

props.name: aspect
props.description:
The shape of the thumbnail, as `Image`'s `aspect`; `natural` keeps the picture's own
proportions (a chat image) and crops nothing.

props.name: caption
props.description: Muted text under the picture, e.g. when.

props.name: external
props.description: Opens in a new tab: adds `target="_blank"` and `rel="noreferrer"`.

props.name: href
props.description: Makes the whole tile one link, named as the button form is; an in-app path goes through `LinkProvider`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: A short line on the bottom edge of the picture, on the media scrim: who posted it, or "Earlier".

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: onClick
props.description:
Makes the whole tile one button; open a `Lightbox` from it. Without it (or `href`) the
tile is a plain, non-interactive block.

props.name: onRemove
props.description:
Adds a round remove button on the picture's top-right corner, named `removeLabel` and `alt`: a
photo attached to a form, until it is sent. It is its own button, beside the tile's, so a tile
with `onClick` still opens its `Lightbox`.

props.name: removeLabel
props.description: The remove button's word, before `alt` in its name and alone as its tooltip.

props.name: src
props.description: The thumbnail, a local path or a data URL. Left out, or if it fails to load, a placeholder shows.

props.name: video
props.description: Draws a play mark on the thumbnail: the tile opens a video, not a photo. Say so in `alt` too.

props.name: width
props.description: `sm` 96px, `md` 160px or `lg` 256px wide; `full` fills the parent (a tile in a grid).

Menu.name: Menu
Menu.description:
A button that opens a short list of actions: the overflow menu at the end of a row, a card header
or a page header. Keep the one main action in view beside it and put the rest here, the `danger`
one last. `items` are data: each a `label` with `onSelect`, or a link with `href` (`external` for
a new tab), an optional leading `icon`, `tone="danger"` and `disabled`.

`trigger="icon"` (the default) is a ghost three-dot button named by `label`; `trigger="button"` is
an outline button reading `label`. The menu opens below the trigger, aligned to its end, and flips
when there is no room. The keyboard is the menu button pattern: Enter, Space or ArrowDown open it
on the first item, ArrowUp on the last; the arrows, Home, End and a letter move; Enter chooses;
Escape closes, and focus goes back to the trigger. `data-*` and `aria-*` land on the trigger.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Opens on mount, for a story or a test that shows the open menu.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: items
props.description: The actions, in order.

props.name: label
props.description: The trigger's accessible name and the menu's. With `trigger="button"` it is the visible text.

props.name: size
props.description:
The trigger's height, the same steps as `IconButton` and `Button`: `sm` inside a row or a card
header. The menu's own text does not change with it.

props.name: trigger
props.description:
`icon` is a ghost square button holding three dots, the overflow menu; `button` is an outline
`Button` with `label` as its text and a chevron after it, for a menu whose name is worth a word.

MetaList.name: MetaList
MetaList.description:
A wrapping row of facts or links in muted small text, joined by a `·`: branch · SHA · date, or a
footer's Privacy · Terms · Email. An item is text, a `Code` or a `TextLink`. The separator is
`aria-hidden` and trails each item but the last, held to its item like a comma, so a wrap leaves
it at the end of a line and never at the start; `separator` swaps it for a `•` or none. An item never breaks inside itself: the
row wraps between items. `mono` sets the whole row in the monospace face, for ids and paths.
While `loading` with no items it draws three word-sized bones.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: mono
props.description: The whole row in the monospace face, for ids and paths.

props.name: separator
props.description: The mark between items: `·`, `•`, or `none` for a gap alone.

Morph.name: Morph
Morph.description:
An element that grows into its counterpart on the next page, and shrinks back on Back, through
the View Transitions API. Wrap the card in the list and the element on the detail page, each with
the same `name` and the record's id as `item`: the browser morphs one into the other over 450 ms. The same
`name` and `item` may appear only once on a page; two on one page and the browser skips the
morph, so a list passes each record's own id. The morph runs only when the change is wrapped in a
view transition: `startPageTransition`, or a router's own option (TanStack Router
`defaultViewTransition: true` on `createRouter`, or `viewTransition` on a `Link`; React Router's
`viewTransition`, Astro's `ClientRouter`). Otherwise, or where the browser has no View
Transitions, it renders and behaves as a plain `<div>`. Inside a `PageFade` the page fades while
this element morphs. While it is named (near the screen) the div is a stacking context, so a
dropdown inside it cannot rise above a sticky header outside it: portal overlays to the body. Under
`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` it swaps with no animation; a router's own transition of the
rest of the page is the router's to quiet. A Morph more than a screen above or below the viewport
carries no transition name until it scrolls near, so a long list costs only what is on screen.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: item
props.description: Which one, usually the record's id. Any text or number; unique on the page for one `name`.

props.name: name
props.description: What the element is, shared by the card and its detail: `"shop"`, `"product"`. Any text.

NavigationProgress.name: NavigationProgress
NavigationProgress.description:
A thin indeterminate bar along the top edge of the viewport, in the accent tone, for a route
change that is under way and has no known length. Pass `loading` from the router's pending state
and render it once per app, beside the page frame. It draws exactly what `loading` says: the bar
while it is true and nothing while it is false. The stylesheet holds it invisible for the first
150ms, so a fast navigation shows nothing. It is fixed to the viewport and overlays the top of
the header, so nothing on the page moves. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` it is a still
bar.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The bar's accessible name.

props.name: loading
props.description: True while a navigation is pending, e.g. from the router's state.

NotFound.name: NotFound
NotFound.description:
404: the page is not there. `numeral` draws a large "404" above the title, for a site whose 404
is a designed page; the digits are fixed. Off, the page is the title and copy alone.

props.name: actions
props.description:
The page's own buttons, before "Back to home", which turns outline beside them. This is the one
way to a button worded differently; there is no label prop.

props.name: children
props.description: Replaces the default body copy.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: numeral
props.description: Draws a large "404" above the title. Off by default. The digits are fixed: there is no text prop.

props.name: title
props.description: Replaces the default heading.

Offline.name: Offline
Offline.description: The device has no connection. `onRetry` adds a "Try again" button, unless `actions` replaces it.

props.name: actions
props.description:
The page's own buttons, before "Back to home", which turns outline beside them. This is the one
way to a button worded differently; there is no label prop.

props.name: children
props.description: Replaces the default body copy.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Adds a "Try again" button that calls it, unless `actions` replaces the button.

props.name: title
props.description: Replaces the default heading.

OutlineRegion.name: OutlineRegion
OutlineRegion.description:
An accent outline over one area of a picture, such as a screenshot's ignored or flagged region.
`rect` is in the picture's own units and `within` is the picture's full size in the same units;
the box is placed in percent of them, so it sits right at any scale. Put it in a `RegionFrame`,
over the picture. `label` is a small tag in its top-left
corner; `hatched` stripes the inside, for an area that is left out. It takes no pointer events,
so it never blocks the picture or a layer drawn over it.

props.name: hatched
props.description: Stripes the inside, for an area left out (ignored, masked).

props.name: label
props.description: A short tag in the top-left corner: where the area came from, or what it is.

props.name: rect
props.description: The area, in the picture's own units.

props.name: within
props.description: The picture's full size, in the same units as `rect`.

Overline.name: Overline
Overline.description:
Small all-caps label above a group. `span`, text-xs semibold uppercase, tertiary. `tone`,
`numeric`, `mono` and `align` are opt-in, as on `Text`.

props.name: align
props.description:
Set the text at `start`, `center` or `end` of its block. The run becomes block-level, so the
alignment has a box to act on (a table header cell, a right-hand column).

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render (each role has a semantic default); the other props follow it.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: mono
props.description: The monospace face, for an id, a path or a command.

props.name: numeric
props.description: Tabular figures, so a column of amounts lines up.

props.name: tone
props.description:
The ink: `neutral`, the default, is the role's own; `muted` and `accent` set the hierarchy of
the text; `positive`, `warn`, `danger` and `info` say what a run means (see `TextTone`).

PageFade.name: PageFade
PageFade.description:
The page's content area, cross-faded by the View Transitions API when the route changes. Wrap
what changes between pages, once per page. With no `name` the fade is the browser's own
cross-fade of the whole viewport; the frame around the content (header, footer) stays still
because it is the same on both pages. A `name` names this box so it fades apart from the page,
for a second region; a named region is captured at its full height, so name only a region no
taller than the screen, and give each named one on a page its own `name`.
The fade runs only when the navigation is wrapped in a view transition: `startPageTransition`,
or a router's own option (TanStack Router `viewTransition`, React Router's `viewTransition` prop,
Astro's `ClientRouter`). Otherwise, or where the browser has no View Transitions, it renders
and behaves as a plain `<div>`. A named PageFade is a stacking context, so a dropdown inside it
cannot rise above a sticky header outside it: portal overlays to the body. The default one is
not. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the content swaps with no fade; a named one quiets
only its own box, and a router's own transition of the rest of the page is the router's to quiet.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: name
props.description: A view-transition name for this box, a CSS identifier (letters, digits, `-`, `_`), for a region no taller than the screen that fades apart from the page.

PageHeader.name: PageHeader
PageHeader.description:
The top of a page: breadcrumbs, title, description, actions and tabs. Its fixed bottom margin puts
every page's first block at the same y; as a direct child of a `Stack` it has none, so the Stack's
gap is the only space under it.
While `loading` it is the owner of the wait: what it has is drawn and an empty title is a bone.

props.name: actions
props.description: Right of the title on `sm` and up, below it on a phone.

props.name: breadcrumbs
props.description: A `Breadcrumbs` above the title.

props.name: description
props.description: The lede under the title: a `Lead`, so it outranks the body text after it.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: tabs
props.description: A `Tabs` (or similar) under the title.

props.name: title
props.description: The page's `h1`.

PageHeading.name: PageHeading
PageHeading.description:
Page title. `h1`, text-3xl/9 bold (text-4xl/10 from `sm`), tight, primary text: well above the
`Lead` under it and the body text after it, so the page's title reads first.

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render (each role has a semantic default); the other props follow it.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

Pagination.name: Pagination
Pagination.description:
Page links for a long list: Previous, the page numbers and Next, in a `<nav>` named by `label`.
Each is a link to `pageHref(page)`, drawn by the app's router link through `LinkProvider`, so the
page lives in the URL and back, a new tab and a shared link all work. The current page is a link
with `aria-current="page"`. Below `sm` the numbers give way to `pageLabel` ("Page 2 of 4").
Renders nothing for one page. The count line ("21 to 40 of 312") is the caller's `Caption`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the `<nav>`. Two pagers on a page (above and below a list) each need their own.

props.name: nextLabel
props.description: The next-page link's text.

props.name: page
props.description: The page shown, from 1. Drawn clamped into `1` to `pageCount`.

props.name: pageCount
props.description: How many pages there are. One or none draws nothing.

props.name: pageHref
props.description: The URL of one page, called for every link drawn: `(page) => (page > 1 ? `?page=${page}` : "?")`.

props.name: pageLabel
props.description: The summary shown in place of the numbers below `sm`. Default: `Page 2 of 4`.

props.name: previousLabel
props.description: The previous-page link's text.

Pill.name: Pill
Pill.description:
A small tinted label whose `tone` says what it means; `dot` adds a leading dot in the pill's own
text colour, `round` swaps the rounded-md corners for a full pill shape, and `size` steps the
text (with none, it takes its container's). `name` makes it two-tone, `name: value`: the name
keeps the tone's tint and the children, the value, sit on the surface beside it. `href` makes it
a link (the app's router link through `LinkProvider` for an in-app path, else a plain `<a>`;
`external` opens a new tab) and `onClick` makes it
a button, each with a hover dim and the focus ring. `onRemove` adds an x button after the text
(named by `removeLabel`), a separate button beside a link or button pill rather than nested in
it. `title` is its tooltip and description; a plain pill with one takes a tab stop. While
`loading` with no text yet it is a bone of its size.

props.name: children
props.description: The pill's text; while `loading`, none yet draws the pill as a bone of its size.

props.name: dot
props.description: A leading dot in the pill's own text colour.

props.name: external
props.description: Opens in a new tab: adds `target="_blank"` and `rel="noreferrer"`.

props.name: href
props.description: Makes the pill a link to this URL; an in-app path goes through the app's `LinkProvider`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: name
props.description:
The name half of a two-tone `name: value` pill: `children` is the value. The name keeps the
tone's tint and the value sits on a plain surface beside it, in a hairline border. Keep the
name to a word or two (`Weight`, `Sleep`).

props.name: onClick
props.description: A Pill that is a button: runs `onClick`. Defaults to `type="button"`.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: Adds a small x button after the text that calls this: for a chip the reader can drop (an attachment, a filter). It sits beside a link or button pill, never inside it.

props.name: removeLabel
props.description: The x button's accessible name and tooltip: `Remove invoice.pdf`. Required with `onRemove`.

props.name: round
props.description: A full pill shape in place of the rounded-md corners.

props.name: size
props.description:
`sm` is smaller text, for a dense row; `lg` larger, beside a heading. Left out, a Pill takes
the size of the `Card`, `ListRow` or `Table` it sits in, else `md`.

props.name: title
props.description:
The detail behind a pill whose text is short or cut off (the full status, a date): its tooltip
on hover, keyboard focus and a tap, and its description. A plain pill with a title is focusable.

props.name: tone
props.description:
What the pill means: `neutral`, `info`, `positive`, `warn` or `danger`, or `accent` for a
category that is none of those.

ProgressBar.name: ProgressBar
ProgressBar.description:
A thin horizontal bar with a filled share, for progress toward a total. `value` is held
between 0 and `max`. `label` names what it measures, for a screen reader, which also hears the percentage.
While `loading` it is one bone the bar's size, since 0 is a real value.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: What the bar measures, for a screen reader, which also hears the percentage.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: max
props.description: The value that fills the bar; `value` is drawn as its share of this. Defaults to 100.

props.name: size
props.description: The bar's height: `sm` 6px, `md` 8px, `lg` 12px.

props.name: tone
props.description:
What the progress means: `accent` (the default) plain progress, `positive` done or on track,
`warn` at risk, `danger` over a limit or failed.

props.name: value
props.description: How far along, held between 0 and `max`.

Prose.name: Prose
Prose.description:
Long-form content, for a docs page or an article. A block (`div`) that sets the long line height
(leading-7) on itself and puts the text roles inside it on the prose scale: `Text` text-base/7
(the size it is outside, on a longer line), `SectionHeading` text-2xl/8, `SubsectionHeading` `lg` text-2xl/8,
`md` text-xl/7 and `sm` text-base/7 (a semibold line at body size), and the box of a `Callout`
text-base/7. Every other role keeps its size. Nothing outside a `Prose` changes, and a `Dialog`,
`Drawer` or `EmptyState` inside one is back on the app scale. An app screen never uses it: wrap the
body of a docs page or an article, inside a `ProseLayout`, a `SidebarLayout` or anywhere else.
Its blocks (`Section`s, paragraphs) are a `Stack`'s gap apart, as they would be in a `Stack`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

ProseLayout.name: ProseLayout
ProseLayout.description:
A text page: header, then `children` stacked `gap` apart (`md` by default), all in one column that
starts at the Container's left edge (it is not re-centred, so the title does not jump). `width`
sets the column: `narrow` (`max-w-3xl`, the default) is a reading measure; `wide` (`max-w-5xl`) and
`full` (the Container's whole width) suit a page that is not long prose, such as a pricing page.
Paragraphs (`Text`) and the header's lede keep their own reading measure whatever the width.
Unlike `FormLayout` the header sits inside the column, so its `actions` stay beside the text
instead of at the Container's far edge. While `loading` it owns the wait and passes it to everything inside, the header too.

props.name: actions
props.description: Right of the title on `sm` and up, below it on a phone.

props.name: breadcrumbs
props.description: A `Breadcrumbs` above the title.

props.name: description
props.description: The lede under the title: a `Lead`, so it outranks the body text after it.

props.name: gap
props.description: The space between blocks: `xs` gap-2, `sm` gap-4, `md` gap-6, `lg` gap-8, `xl` gap-12 (gap-16 from `sm`).

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: tabs
props.description: A `Tabs` (or similar) under the title.

props.name: title
props.description: The page's `h1`.

props.name: width
props.description: The column's width: `narrow` max-w-3xl, `wide` max-w-5xl, `full` the Container's width.

Radio.name: Radio
Radio.description: One option of a `RadioGroup`: a `label` and, under it, an optional `hint`. Click the label or the circle. While `loading` the circle is a bone.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables this radio alone.

props.name: hint
props.description: A muted line under the label that says more. It is the radio's `aria-describedby`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The text beside the circle.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: value
props.description: What the group's `value` becomes when this one is chosen.

RadioGroup.name: RadioGroup
RadioGroup.description:
A named group of radios, one chosen. The `label` names the group; `hint` is a muted line under
the options that says more (the group's description); an `error` replaces it with a red line
(`role="alert"`) and marks the group invalid. Give it `value` and `onChange`, or
`defaultValue` and let it keep the choice. `name` posts the choice in a form.
The arrow keys move between the radios and choose, and the group is one tab stop. `size` sizes
every radio in the group, the same scale as a `Checkbox`. While `loading` the labels are drawn and
each circle is a bone.

props.name: children
props.description: The `Radio`s.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The `value` chosen to begin with, when the group keeps its own choice.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every radio.

props.name: error
props.description: Shown under the options in red with `role="alert"`; marks the group invalid. Like `Field`'s `error`.

props.name: hint
props.description: A muted line under the options that says more; it describes the group. Replaced by `error`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The group's visible name, above the options.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field the choice posts under.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the chosen radio's `value`.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the choice required: the group is `aria-required`, and a form will not submit with no option chosen.

props.name: size
props.description:
The size of every radio in the group: `sm` is `text-xs` and a smaller circle, `lg` `text-base`
and a larger one.

props.name: value
props.description: The `value` of the chosen radio.

readColourScheme.name: readColourScheme
readColourScheme.description: The stored choice, else the system preference. `fallback` (default `"light"`) is for when neither is available: server rendering, or storage that throws with no `matchMedia`.

refreshMorphs.name: refreshMorphs
refreshMorphs.description:
Measures every mounted Morph again, at once, so a card a router has just scrolled on screen
carries its transition name before the browser captures the new page. Call it right after the
router restores scroll, when that happens after the render: TanStack Router restores scroll on
`onRendered`, a few microtasks after the commit, which is too late for Morph to see on its own.

```ts
const router = createRouter({ routeTree, defaultViewTransition: true, scrollRestoration: true });
router.subscribe("onRendered", () => refreshMorphs());
```

Subscribe after the router is created, so its own scroll restore runs first. A restore in a
layout effect, during the commit, needs no call. It takes no arguments and does nothing on the
server or where there is no IntersectionObserver.

RegionFrame.name: RegionFrame
RegionFrame.description: A picture with a hairline edge, and `children` laid over it: the `OutlineRegion`s that mark its areas. Every other prop goes to the `` (`onLoad`, `loading`, `data-*`), so the app can read the picture's own size for `within`. It sizes as `Image` does. `width` is `full` (the parent's width) or 96, 160 or 256px. `aspect` `natural` keeps the picture's own proportions; any other shape letterboxes it (contain, never a crop) on the inset surface, centred and never scaled up, and the regions are laid over the picture itself, not the box, so each stays on its spot. A letterboxed picture needs its own size: a screenshot has one; an SVG needs `width` and `height` on its root, not only a `viewBox`.

props.name: alt
props.description: What the picture shows; `""` for one that only decorates.

props.name: aspect
props.description: The box's shape: `natural` is the picture's own; any other letterboxes the picture inside it.

props.name: children
props.description: The `OutlineRegion`s over the picture.

props.name: src
props.description: The picture.

props.name: width
props.description: How wide the frame is: `full` fills its parent; `sm`, `md` and `lg` are 96, 160 and 256px, capped at the parent's width.

schemeClass.name: schemeClass
schemeClass.description: The class for `scheme`: what to render on `<html>` on the server so the first paint is right. `""` for the default light scheme.

ScrollStrip.name: ScrollStrip
ScrollStrip.description:
A single row of items that scrolls sideways when it runs past the width of its parent, with a
thin themed scrollbar and the items snapping into place: a strip of `MediaTile`s or `Avatar`s.
Items never shrink or wrap. The strip takes the keyboard focus, so the arrow keys scroll it
without a pointer. A grid that wraps is a `CardGrid` or a `Cluster`.

props.name: children
props.description: The items, one after another: `MediaTile`s, `Avatar`s. They keep their own width.

props.name: gap
props.description: The space between items, as `Cluster`'s `gap`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the strip for a screen reader, e.g. "Recent statuses".

Section.name: Section
Section.description:
A `<section>` Stack with an optional title (which names it) and `actions`. Its blocks are `gap`
apart, from where it sits as in a `Stack`. `level` is the title's heading level, one below the
heading that holds the section (an `h2` on the page), and a heading inside it (a `Card`'s title)
is one below that. A line between two sections is a `Divider` in the `Stack` that holds them.

`size` picks the scale:
- `md` (default): a page's section. A `SectionHeading` title with `actions` at the end of its row;
  `rule` draws a hairline under the row, `overline` a small label above the title and
  `description` a muted line under it.
- `sm`: the small titled group inside a page, a card, a drawer or a side panel (a panel's "Flaky"
  block, a card's "Ignore areas"): the title small and all-caps like a `Card`'s, the blocks `xs`
  apart. Never build one from a `Stack as="section"` and an `Overline`.
- `lg`: a landing page's section under the `Hero`: a mono `overline` kicker, the title at display
  size, `description` as a `Lead` and `actions` under it as its calls to action, the opening
  capped at the reading measure at the left edge, the blocks `lg` apart. It ignores the prose scale.

props.name: actions
props.description: Buttons or links: at the end of the title row, or under the description at `size="lg"`.

props.name: description
props.description: The line under the title, outside the heading: a muted line at `md`, a `Lead` at `lg`.

props.name: gap
props.default: xs at `size="sm"`, lg at `size="lg"`; else xs inside a `Card`, `Dialog`, `Drawer`, `BottomSheet`, `Callout` or `ListRow`, else md
props.description: The space between blocks: `xs` gap-2, `sm` gap-4, `md` gap-6, `lg` gap-8, `xl` gap-12 (gap-16 from `sm`).

props.name: id
props.description:
Makes the section a link target: `#<id>` scrolls to its heading, which stops below the sticky
AppShell header, as every `id` inside the shell does; write no `scroll-margin`. Needs a `title`:
with no title the heading that carries it is not rendered.
The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: level
props.default: one below the heading that holds the section: 2 on the page
props.description: The title's heading level, 2 to 6. It does not change how the title looks.

props.name: overline
props.description: A small label above the title, in the same `<header>` (mono at `size="lg"`). Needs a `title`.

props.name: rule
props.description:
A hairline under the title row across the section's width, `actions` included. Needs a
`title` or `actions`.

props.name: size
props.description:
`sm` a small titled group inside a page, a card or a panel, its title small and all-caps
and its blocks `xs` apart; `md` a page's section; `lg` a landing page's section, a display
title under a mono kicker, a `Lead`, then its calls to action.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading at the top, which names the section.

props.name: width
props.description:
Caps the column: `compact` max-w-md (one card or one picture's column), `narrow` max-w-3xl (a
reading measure), `wide` max-w-5xl, `full` the parent's whole width, `default` sets nothing.

SectionHeading.name: SectionHeading
SectionHeading.description:
Top-level section header. `h2`, text-xl/7 semibold, primary text (text-base/6 under an
`AppShell density="compact"`, text-2xl/8 semibold tight inside a `Prose`). `rule` sets
a hairline under it (the `Divider` line colour) with the space either side of
the line built in. `description` is a muted line under the heading, outside the `<h2>`, so the
heading's name stays the title; the rule then sits under the description.

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render (each role has a semantic default); the other props follow it.

props.name: description
props.description: A muted line under the heading that says more. It is a paragraph beside the heading, not part of its name.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: rule
props.description: A hairline under the heading, with the space either side of it built in.

SegmentedControl.name: SegmentedControl
SegmentedControl.description:
A joined pill group where one option is filled: a mode or a range chosen in place. `items` are
`{ value, label }` buttons (`value` and `onChange` are the caller's state; the arrow keys, Home
and End move the choice) or links (`href`, an in-app one drawn by the app's router `<Link>` through `LinkProvider`;
`value` marks the current one, which gets `aria-current`). An item may carry a `count`, and a
button one `disabledReason` (it stays reachable by the arrows and its reason is a tooltip) or a bare `disabled`; `disabled` on the group disables every
option. `label` names the group. `size` matches the height of a `Button` of the same size.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Every option is disabled, e.g. until the page has hydrated.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: items
props.description: The options in order: `{ value, label }` buttons, or links (`href`), the current link marked by its `selected` or by a `value` equal to the group's. Either may carry a `count`; a button may be `disabled`.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name of the group.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the option's `value` when one is chosen, by click or arrow key.

props.name: size
props.description: The control's height and text, on the scale of a `Button`.

props.name: value
props.description: The `value` of the current option; for links, an alternative to `selected` on the item.

Select.name: Select
Select.description:
A native `<select>` styled like `Input`, keeping the browser's own arrow, over its `items`. Takes
`size` and `width` too: inside a `Field` it fills the row, and on its own it is as wide as its
longest choice. The `ref` reaches the `<select>`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the select; say why in its `Field` hint.

props.name: items
props.description: The choices, in order.

props.name: name
props.description: The key the value posts under in a form.

props.name: ref
props.description: The `<select>` itself, for focus control.

props.name: size
width
props.description: As an `Input`'s `width`.

Show.name: Show
Show.description:
Shows its children only from a width up (`from`) or only below it (`below`), by CSS alone: the same markup on the server and the client, with no script. Hidden is `display: none`, so the content is out of the accessibility tree and the tab order too. Shown, the wrapper adds no box, so the children sit in the parent's row, grid or Stack and take its gap. Content that only fits a wide screen is in a `Show from`; its narrow-screen form is in a `Show below` at the same breakpoint. Hidden content stays mounted, so two `Show`s of the same content mount it twice: a stateful panel shown at every width with a fold is a `SideColumn asideLabel`. `as="span"` is for phrasing content (inside a `

` or a button row).

props.name: as
props.description: The element: `div`, or `span` inside phrasing content.

props.name: below
props.description: Shown below this width, gone from it up.

props.name: from
props.description: Shown from this width up, gone below it.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

SidebarLayout.name: SidebarLayout
SidebarLayout.description:
An `aside` of links (the rail) beside the `children` canvas, in the Container the shell already gives every
page (a plain `<AppShell>`, no `bleed`): the rail starts at the header logo's x and the canvas
ends at the header's right edge. The rail has no background and no border, so it is a list of
links on the page; a `Tabs orientation="vertical"` is its content. From `md` it is `w-56` with
the canvas filling the rest, and it stays in view under the shell's header as a long page scrolls;
a rail taller than the screen scrolls itself, so its last link is reachable. Below `md` it stacks
above the canvas and nothing sticks. A long rail sets `asideLabel`:
below `md` it then folds behind a disclosure of that name, closed, so the page comes first on a
phone, and from `md` it is the same rail; `asideLabel` also names the rail's `<aside>` landmark.
Once the page has
loaded, a rail that scrolls shows its current link (the one with `aria-current`) in view, and the
folded disclosure reads `asideLabel` and the current link's name ("All components: Button"); both
need the layout to hydrate.
While `loading` the canvas waits (the rail is navigation, drawn as itself) and the layout owns
the wait.

props.name: aside
props.description: The links beside the canvas, usually a `Tabs orientation="vertical"`.

props.name: asideLabel
props.description:
Folds the rail behind a disclosure with this name below `md` (a long rail), and names the rail's
`<aside>` landmark. Left out, the rail is always open and the aside is unnamed.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

SideColumn.name: SideColumn
SideColumn.description:
A main area beside a side column, in the Container the page already has: from `lg` the `aside`
is `asideWidth` on the right and `children` take the room left; below `lg` the aside stacks under
`children`. It sets no page width, padding or header of its own, so it sits inside a layout, a
`Card` or a panel. `asideWidth` is `sm` (18rem), `md` (24rem) or `third` (one third of the row,
the main area two thirds: the split `DetailLayout` draws). A rail of links on the left is
`SidebarLayout`.

`asideLabel` is for an aside that should not take the phone's screen: below `lg` it folds,
closed, behind a native disclosure of that name, and from `lg` it is the same column, always
shown. The aside stays mounted while folded, so a conversation or a draft inside it is kept.

`sticky` keeps the aside in view from `lg` as a long page scrolls: it sticks under AppShell's
header and, if it is taller than the room left, scrolls itself (a tab stop named by `asideLabel`)
so its end stays reachable.

props.name: aside
props.description: The side column: `asideWidth` wide on the right from `lg`, under `children` below it.

props.name: asideLabel
props.description: Folds the aside behind a disclosure with this name below `lg`, and names the `<aside>` landmark. Left out, the aside is always shown and unnamed.

props.name: asideWidth
props.description: The aside's width from `lg`: `sm` 18rem, `md` 24rem, or `third`, one third of the row.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: sticky
props.description:
From `lg`, keeps the aside in view under the header as the page scrolls; an aside taller than
the screen scrolls inside itself.

SiteFooter.name: SiteFooter
SiteFooter.description:
The footer a site puts in `AppShell`'s `footer` slot: the site's mark linked home with a contact
line beside it, a row of the site's own links (Privacy, Terms, GitHub), then lines of fine print.
It is not a `<footer>`: the shell draws the one `contentinfo` landmark around its slot. No link
columns, newsletter form or social icons: a site footer is this and nothing else.

props.name: brand
props.description: The site's mark (a wordmark, a logo), linked to `brandHref`. Left out, there is no brand.

props.name: brandHref
props.description: Where the brand links. Needs `brand`.

props.name: brandLabel
props.description: Names the brand link for assistive tech ("PixelSlash home"). Needs `brand`.

props.name: children
props.description: A sentence at body size beside the brand: the contact line ("Email hello@...").

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: links
props.description: The site's own links (Privacy, Terms, GitHub, a mail address), one wrapping row.

props.name: notes
props.description: Lines of fine print under the links (a licence, a trademark, a credit), one paragraph each.

SiteSearch.name: SiteSearch
SiteSearch.description:
The site's search: a header button that opens a dialog with a search field over a list of links
to the pages that match. Put it in `AppShell`'s `controls` and pass every page as `items`. Ctrl+K
(⌘ K on a Mac) opens it from anywhere on the page, and the button shows that key. Typing filters
by name, then by `keywords`, then by description; Enter opens the first result, the arrow keys
move through them, and Esc closes it and puts focus back where it was. Render it once per page.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: items
props.description: Every page to search, in the order ties are listed (the rail's order).

props.name: label
props.description:
The dialog's title and the phone's icon button's accessible name: "Search components". The wide
button is named by its own text, "Search".

props.name: resultsLabel
props.description: The name of the list of matches, for an app in another language.

SortableItem.name: SortableItem
SortableItem.description:
One row of a `SortableList`: a grip handle, the title, and an optional meta line under it. A
pointer drags the row itself; the handle ("Reorder <title>") is how a keyboard or screen reader
starts a move.

props.name: children
props.description: A meta line under the title: `Pill`s, an `Avatar`.

props.name: id
props.description:
The item's id, reported in a move.
The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: title
props.description: Its one line; also what a screen reader announces while it is dragged.

SortableList.name: SortableList
SortableList.description:
A list the user puts in order: items under section headings, moved by dragging a row or from the
keyboard (each row's grip handle, Enter, the arrow keys, Enter to drop, Escape to cancel). A drop
reports `onReorder` with the item, the section it lands in and the item it lands next to; the app
applies it to its own data. The list never reorders itself: it shows what its children say.

Its children are `SortableSection`s, or `SortableItem`s directly for a list with no sections, each
a direct child (map your data straight to them). Moving an item into another section is how the
app changes its group, such as a ticket's priority. Two lists on one page never take each other's
items.

props.name: children
props.description: `SortableSection`s, or `SortableItem`s for a list with no sections.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The list's accessible name, read by a screen reader.

props.name: onReorder
props.description: Called once per drop with the move; apply it to your data.

SortableSection.name: SortableSection
SortableSection.description:
One group of a `SortableList` under a heading that shows its title and how many items it holds.
An empty section still takes a drop: it shows a quiet "Drop here" row in place of items.

props.name: children
props.description: Its `SortableItem`s, each a direct child. With none it shows a quiet `emptyLabel` row.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: The quiet row an empty section shows, where a drop lands.

props.name: id
props.description:
The section's id, reported as `section` in a move that lands in it.
The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading over its items.

SplitBar.name: SplitBar
SplitBar.description:
A bar split between two parties, `a` on the left and `b` on the right, each sized by its share of
`a + b`. `label` names the split for a screen reader, which hears both percentages; give `names`
(left, right) so it hears whose is whose. Put the parties' names under the bar yourself.
While `loading` it is one bone the bar's size, since 0 is a real value.

props.name: a
props.description: The left party's amount; its share is `a` over `a + b`.

props.name: b
props.description: The right party's amount; its share is `b` over `a + b`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: What the split is, for a screen reader, which hears it before both percentages.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: names
props.description: The left and right parties, spoken before their percentages.

props.name: size
props.description: The bar's height: `sm` 6px, `md` 8px, `lg` 12px.

props.name: toneA
props.description: The left part's colour, by what it means (`accent`, `positive`, `warn` or `danger`). Defaults to "danger".

props.name: toneB
props.description: The right part's colour, by what it means (`accent`, `positive`, `warn` or `danger`). Defaults to "positive".

Stack.name: Stack
Stack.description:
A vertical column of blocks a fixed `gap` apart: `xs` between lines of text (a heading and the
line under it), `sm` inside a group, `md` between blocks, `lg` between groups, `xl` between a page's top-level blocks
(`gap-12`, `sm:gap-16`: the one responsive page rhythm). Left out, the gap comes from where the
Stack sits: `xs` inside a `Card`, `Dialog`, `Drawer`, `BottomSheet`, `Callout` or `ListRow`, and
`md` on the page.

`width` caps the column: `compact` is the width of one card or one picture's column (28rem),
`narrow` is a reading measure, `wide` is wider again, `full` is the parent's whole width and
`default` sets nothing. A capped Stack starts at its parent's left edge (it is never re-centred),
so its first line lines up with every other block on the page. A width cap on any one block (a
`Card`, an `Image`) is a Stack around it.

`align="start"` keeps each child at its own width, capped at the column's (a `Button` under a
form's fields); left out, every child spans the column.

`divided` draws a line between each pair of children and sets them touching, with no gap: it is
for rows that carry their own padding (`ListRow`s in a `Card flush`). Space and a line between
blocks is a `Divider` in the Stack instead.

`rowFrom` turns the column into a row from `sm`, `md` or `lg` (a column below it): the blocks sit
side by side, `gap` apart, and a `ClusterGrow` around one of them takes the width left. Without it the
Stack is always a column; a row that is a row at every width is a `Cluster`.

`as` is a closed set: `div` (default), `section`, `form`, `ul` or `ol`. A `form` takes the form
props (`onSubmit`, `action`, `method`, `noValidate`, ...). A `ul` or `ol` is drawn with no
markers and its children are `<li>`s, as in `BulletList` and `Timeline`: the Stack does not wrap
them, so a child is one list item and `Text as="li"` or a bare `<li>` both work. A `ul` or `ol`
takes `empty` (an `EmptyState`, one muted line here), drawn in place of the list when it has no
children.

props.name: align
props.description:
Where the children sit across the column: `stretch` spans it, `start` keeps each child at its
own width (a `Button` under a form's fields).

props.name: as
props.description: The element: `div`, `section`, `form` (takes the form's props), `ul` or `ol` (no markers; each child is an `<li>`).

props.name: divided
props.description:
A line between each pair of children, which then touch (no gap): rows that carry their own
padding. Space and a line between blocks is a `Divider` in the Stack instead.

props.name: empty
props.description: Drawn in place of the list when it has no children: an `EmptyState`.

props.name: gap
props.default: xs inside a `Card`, `Dialog`, `Drawer`, `BottomSheet`, `Callout` or `ListRow`, else md
props.description: The space between blocks: `xs` gap-2, `sm` gap-4, `md` gap-6, `lg` gap-8, `xl` gap-12 (gap-16 from `sm`).

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: rowFrom
props.description:
Turns the column into a row from this breakpoint (`sm`, `md` or `lg`), a column below it: a main
area beside a side column on a wide screen, stacked on a phone. In the row the blocks sit side by side
the same `gap` apart and are as tall as the tallest; wrap the one that takes the width left in a
`ClusterGrow`. Left out, the Stack is always a column.

props.name: width
props.description:
Caps the column: `compact` max-w-md (one card or one picture's column), `narrow` max-w-3xl (a
reading measure), `wide` max-w-5xl, `full` the parent's whole width, `default` sets nothing.

StackedBar.name: StackedBar
StackedBar.description:
A bar of any number of parts, each sized by its share of the sum, in the order given. A part with
no value is zero wide. `label` names the bar for a screen reader, which hears every part's name
and whole percent (rounded, so they may not add up to exactly 100). `legend` draws a `Legend` under the bar, each part's
