label with its value, so the colours are named in words. While `loading` the bar is one bone (0
is a real value) and the key keeps the names it has, without their values.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: items
props.description: The parts in order, each a `label`, a `value` (its share is the value over the sum) and a `tone`.

props.name: label
props.description: What the bar shows, for a screen reader, which hears it before every part's name and percent.

props.name: legend
props.description: Draw the key under the bar. Defaults to false.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: size
props.description: The bar's height: `sm` 6px, `md` 8px, `lg` 12px.

startPageTransition.name: startPageTransition
startPageTransition.description:
Run `update` inside a view transition, so a `PageFade` cross-fades. `update` is a synchronous
state change, flushed at once as the browser needs the new DOM; for a router's navigation, which
is async, use the router's own view-transition option instead. Where the browser has
no View Transitions, or the user prefers reduced motion, `update` just runs. Call it from an event
handler, not during render.

StatTile.name: StatTile
StatTile.description:
One headline figure: an uppercase caption over a large tabular-nums value, with an optional
hint line beneath. `tone` colours the value; `accent` adds a bar across the top edge in the same
tone. `trend` draws a small line under the value in the same colour. Pass the value already
formatted. While `loading`, a `label` or `value` not here yet is a bone; the hint and the trend
are drawn only once given.

props.name: accent
props.description: A bar across the top edge in the tone's colour.

props.name: hint
props.description: A muted line under the value.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The small uppercase caption over the value.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: tone
props.description:
What the figure means: `neutral` (the default) a plain figure, `positive` good or on track,
`warn` at risk, `danger` failed or over. Say it in the text too: colour alone says nothing to a
screen reader.

props.name: trend
props.description:
The figure over time, oldest first: a sparkline under the value, in its colour, on a scale
from 0. It is decoration, so say the trend in `hint` as well.

props.name: value
props.description: The figure, already formatted, large and in tabular figures.

Step.name: Step
Step.description: One step of `Steps`: a `title` and the `children` as the detail under it, at its `Steps`' size.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: title
props.description: What to do; `children` is the detail under it.

Steps.name: Steps
Steps.description:
A numbered list of things to do, in order: a `title` and, under it, a line of `children`. The
numbers are counted by CSS, so `Step`s can sit in a fragment or behind a condition and still run
1, 2, 3. For the way into a product ("install, log in, run"), not for progress: nothing here is
done or current. A wizard's progress indicator is a different part.

`size="lg"` is the steps across a landing page: from `md` they sit side by side in equal columns,
each number at feature size over a large title; below `md` they stack. Use it for two to four
steps.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: size
props.description: `md` a small list down a column; `lg` the steps across a landing page from `md` (two to four).

StickyBar.name: StickyBar
StickyBar.description:
A full-width row that sticks under AppShell's header as the page scrolls: a filter or actions
bar, or a viewer's title and its actions. It sits on the surface with a bottom line and pads its
content as the Container pads a page. Put a `Cluster` in it for the row's layout. It spans its
parent, so it belongs at the top of an `AppShell bleed` page; `FullBleedLayout`'s `bar` is one.

props.name: children
props.description: The bar's content, usually one `Cluster` (`justify="between"` for a title and its actions).

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

storeColourScheme.name: storeColourScheme
storeColourScheme.description: Remember `scheme` for the next visit. A storage error is swallowed, so private mode does not crash.

SubsectionHeading.name: SubsectionHeading
SubsectionHeading.description:
Nested header. `h3`, text-lg/7 semibold, primary text. `size` steps it down to `sm` (text-base,
body size set apart by its weight) for a form-group caption or a dense card, or up to `lg`
(text-xl) for a drawer title; `md` is the default. Under an `AppShell density="compact"` each is one step down. Inside a `Prose`
`md` is text-xl/7 (the h3 of a doc), `sm` text-base/7 (the h4: body size, set apart by its weight)
and `lg` text-2xl/8, the size of a `SectionHeading` there. `truncate` keeps it on
one line and cuts it with an ellipsis where its container ends, the full text as the `title`.

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render (each role has a semantic default); the other props follow it.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: size
props.description:
The heading's type size: `sm` is text-base/6, `md` text-lg/7 and `lg` text-xl/7 (one step down
each under an `AppShell density="compact"`).

props.name: truncate
props.description: One line, cut with an ellipsis where the container ends; the full text becomes the `title`.

Switch.name: Switch
Switch.description:
An on/off switch for a setting that takes effect at once, usually by saving it to a server: a
native `<button role="switch" aria-checked>`. The caller owns `checked` and flips it in
`onChange`, or gives `defaultChecked` and the switch keeps its own state. A value sent with a
form is a `Checkbox`, not a Switch. Give it a `label`
(the whole label is the click target), or in a table cell leave the label out and name it with
`aria-label`. `hint` is a muted line under the label; `error` replaces it with a red line
(`role="alert"`) and makes the switch `aria-invalid`. The note is the switch's
`aria-describedby`. `size` is `sm`, `md` (the default) or `lg`. `busy` is for the save in
flight: clicks and keys do nothing, and the switch keeps its colour and its focus.
`disabledReason` blocks it, focusable, with the reason as its tooltip. `disabled` is the native
one, washed out. While `loading` the label is drawn and the track is a bone of its size.

props.name: busy
props.description:
The change is being saved: `aria-busy`, and a click or a key does nothing. It keeps its colour
and its focus, which a native `disabled` would lose when the save starts.

props.name: checked
props.description: Whether it is on, when the caller owns it (with `onChange`).

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Whether it starts on, when the switch keeps its own state.

props.name: disabledReason
props.description:
Why the switch cannot be flipped: it washes out and is blocked (`aria-disabled`; a click,
Enter and Space do nothing) while it keeps its focus, and the reason is its tooltip on hover,
keyboard focus and a tap, read out as its description.

props.name: error
props.description: Replaces the hint with a red line (`role="alert"`) and makes the switch `aria-invalid`.

props.name: hint
props.description: A muted line under the label that says more. It is the switch's `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The text beside the switch; the whole label is a click target.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the next value when the person flips it. Not called while `busy`.

props.name: size
props.description: The label's text size and the switch with it.

Table.name: Table
Table.description:
A list of records in a rounded, bordered card that scrolls sideways on a narrow screen. Compose it
from `TableHead`, `TableBody`, `TableFoot`, `TableRow`, `TableHeaderCell` and `TableCell`. `label`
names the table for assistive tech and is not drawn. Inside a `Card` it is plain: no card of its
own (border, fill and shadow), no tinted head strip and no row hover, only the row dividers. A
column of figures says so once, with `numeric` on its `TableHeaderCell`: its cells then take end
alignment and tabular figures. `size` is the row padding, and the controls in the rows follow it
(`sm` by default). Other props (`id`, `data-*`, `aria-*`) go on the `<table>`. While `loading`, a
body with no rows draws five rows of bones, one per column, and an empty cell draws a bone; the
table keeps its role and its name.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the table for assistive tech; it is not drawn.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: size
props.description: The row padding; the buttons and fields in the rows take the same size.

TableBody.name: TableBody
TableBody.description:
The `<tbody>`: the rows, each with a line above it and, unless the table is in a card, a fill on
hover. With no rows it draws `empty` (an `EmptyState`, one muted line here) in one cell that spans
every column the head declares; the head stays drawn, so the reader sees what the table holds.
In a loading `Table` a body with no rows draws five rows of bones instead, never `empty`.

props.name: empty
props.description: Shown in one full-width cell when there are no rows: an `EmptyState`.

TableCell.name: TableCell
TableCell.description:
A `<td>`. `tone` is the text weight and colour (see `CellTone`; in a `TableFoot` it defaults to
`strong`); `numeric` sets end alignment and tabular figures (a cell under a `numeric` head cell is
numeric already), `mono` a small mono face. `secondary` is a second,
muted line under the content. One rule for wrapping: prose (a cell of plain text) wraps onto more
lines (never narrower than `min-w-48`, so it scrolls the table before it becomes a sliver), a cell
that holds a control or a link takes that content's width, and a `numeric` or `mono` cell (a
figure, a code, a type) never breaks. `truncate` caps a long value's width, cuts it with
an ellipsis on one line and puts the full text in a `title`; the content is then plain text (strings and
numbers), since that is what the title shows. `colSpan` passes through: a cell that
spans the row is a full-width panel (a note under a group), and `align="center"` centres it. A
table with no rows takes `TableBody empty`, not a cell built by hand. `span="full"` spans every
column the head declares, so a panel under a row needs no count. `indent` sets a start-aligned cell in by 1 to 3 levels, for a line under a parent row.
While `loading` an empty cell draws one bone, the width of a short value.

props.name: align
props.default: end for a numeric cell, else start
props.description: The cell's horizontal alignment; `center` for a full-width note.

props.name: colSpan
props.description: How many columns the cell spans; `span="full"` spans them all without a count.

props.name: indent
props.description: Sets the cell in by this many levels (1 to 3), for a line under a parent row. Start-aligned cells only.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: mono
props.description: A small monospace face for a code or a type, and the cell never wraps.

props.name: numeric
props.default: the column's, from a `numeric` head cell
props.description: A figure: end aligned, tabular figures, and the cell never wraps.

props.name: secondary
props.description: A second, muted line under the content.

props.name: span
props.description: `full` spans every column the head declares: a panel under a row, an open row's detail.

props.name: tone
props.description: The text weight and colour (see `CellTone`). In a `TableFoot` it defaults to `strong`.

props.name: truncate
props.description: Caps the width and cuts a long value with an ellipsis on one line, the full text in a `title`. Plain text content only.

TableEditCell.name: TableEditCell
TableEditCell.description:
A `TableCell` whose value opens an editor in place: a cell that holds one `InlineEdit` and
nothing else. It shows `children` as a button with a dotted underline; a click, Enter or Space
swaps it for `renderEditor(close)` and moves the focus into the editor. The editor calls `close`
when it has saved, and Esc closes it: both put the focus back on the value. A press outside it or
Tab out of it closes it too and leaves the focus where it went, so the editor saves its value on
its own change or submit, never on a close. Put the control in the cell itself, not in a popover
of its own, which counts as outside. Takes `TableCell`'s `align`, `tone`, `numeric`, `mono`,
`indent`, `secondary` and `span`. For an edit trigger in a cell that holds other content too, put an
`InlineEdit` in a `TableCell`.

props.name: align
props.default: end for a numeric cell, else start
props.description: The cell's horizontal alignment; `center` for a full-width note.

props.name: children
props.description: The value, shown while closed.

props.name: colSpan
props.description: How many columns the cell spans; `span="full"` spans them all without a count.

props.name: indent
props.description: Sets the cell in by this many levels (1 to 3), for a line under a parent row. Start-aligned cells only.

props.name: label
props.description: What the button does, for a screen reader, heard after the value: "Edit category". It also names the editor.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: mono
props.description: A small monospace face for a code or a type, and the cell never wraps.

props.name: numeric
props.default: the column's, from a `numeric` head cell
props.description: A figure: end aligned, tabular figures, and the cell never wraps.

props.name: renderEditor
props.description: The control that edits the value, drawn while open. `close` shuts it and returns the focus to the value.

props.name: secondary
props.description: A second, muted line under the content.

props.name: span
props.description: `full` spans every column the head declares: a panel under a row, an open row's detail.

props.name: tone
props.description: The text weight and colour (see `CellTone`). In a `TableFoot` it defaults to `strong`.

TableExpandCell.name: TableExpandCell
TableExpandCell.description:
The cell that opens and closes the row it sits in: a small ghost button with a chevron that turns
down when `expanded`, named by `label` (visually hidden) and, with a `count`, the count chip after
it, so it reads "Details, 3". The app holds `expanded` and renders what opens under the row: a
`TableRow` with one `TableCell span="full"`, or indented child rows. Give its column a head of
`<TableHeaderCell label="Details" />`. `aria-controls` names what it opens; other props go on the
`<td>`.

props.name: count
props.description: A count chip after the chevron: how many lines open under the row.

props.name: expanded
props.description: Whether the row is open.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The button's name, visually hidden: "Details".

props.name: onClick
props.description: Opens or closes the row: the app flips `expanded`.

TableFoot.name: TableFoot
TableFoot.description:
The `<tfoot>`: totals and subtotals. Its cells are strong by default and each row has a firmer
line above it, alone and in a card alike. Put it after `TableBody`; a row of it takes
no `tone`.

TableGroupRow.name: TableGroupRow
TableGroupRow.description:
A full-width group header in the body: a tinted row with a `label` that spans every column the
head declares (or `colSpan` columns), and optional `trailing` content at the far end (a count, a
subtotal, a small button). The group's rows follow it. For a panel of other content across the
whole row, use a `TableCell span="full"` instead.

props.name: colSpan
props.description: How many columns the header spans.

props.name: label
props.description: The group's name, at the start of the row.

props.name: trailing
props.description: Content at the far end of the row: a count, a subtotal, a small button.

TableHead.name: TableHead
TableHead.description: The `<thead>`: small uppercase column titles, on a tinted strip unless the table is in a card. Holds one `TableRow` of `TableHeaderCell`s.

TableHeaderCell.name: TableHeaderCell
TableHeaderCell.description:
A column title, `<th scope="col">`. `numeric` declares a column of figures, once: the title and
every cell under it take end alignment and tabular figures. A column with nothing to show in its
head (a row's actions) takes `label` instead of `children`: the name a screen reader hears
("Actions"), visually hidden so the head keeps its column. `sort` and `onSort` make the column
sortable: the title becomes a button that asks for the next direction, and the column says where
it stands with `aria-sort`. The app sorts its rows; the table never does.

props.name: align
props.description: The title's horizontal alignment; `end` over a column of buttons, `center` over a centred column.

props.name: label
props.description: The column's name for a screen reader, visually hidden, for a column with no visible title (a row's actions).

props.name: numeric
props.description: A column of figures: this title and the cells under it are end aligned, the cells in tabular figures.

props.name: onSort
props.description: Called with the next direction on a click: `none` goes to `ascending`, then each click flips it.

props.name: sort
props.description:
Where this column stands: `ascending`, `descending`, or `none` when the table is sorted by
another column. The app sorts its rows and passes it back; one sorted column at a time.

TableRow.name: TableRow
TableRow.description:
A `<tr>`, `relative`: the anchor a `TextLink stretch` (with `href`) stretches to. Any other link, button or
control in the row (a `TextLink`, a `Button`, a `Checkbox`) sits above that link and is clickable
on its own, with no class from the caller. Use it in the head and the
body. In the body it also draws the line above the row and, unless the table is in a card, the hover
fill. `selected` marks the current row (the one open beside the table, the one being edited): the
`ListRow` selected fill and `aria-current`, the row whose detail is open, not a multi-select; it wins over `tone` and `stripe`. `tone` marks the row's status (see `RowTone`): a stripe on the leading edge and a soft fill,
or `muted` to fade it. A toned row keeps its fill on hover (the status stays readable), so a
linked row's link, not a hover fill, says it is clickable. `stripe` is the stripe alone, in the
`TextTone` colours (the first five names of a `StackedBar` segment's `VizTone`), with no fill: the row keeps its hover
and its own look. Give `tone` or `stripe`, not both. Body rows only; colour alone does not say it,
so name the status in a cell too (a `Pill`). A bold subtotal is not a tone: a total of the whole
table is a `TableFoot` row, and a subtotal among the body's rows is `emphasis`, the same look.

props.name: emphasis
props.description: A subtotal in the body: the look of a `TableFoot` row, with strong cells, a firmer line above and no hover. Give only one of `tone`, `stripe` and `emphasis`.

props.name: selected
props.description: The row in view (its detail open beside the table): the selected fill and `aria-current`. Body rows only.

props.name: stripe
props.description: A stripe on the leading edge in this tone, with no fill. Give only one of `tone`, `stripe` and `emphasis`.

props.name: tone
props.description: The row's status: a stripe on the leading edge plus the tone's soft fill, or `muted` to fade the row. Give only one of `tone`, `stripe` and `emphasis`.

Tabs.name: Tabs
Tabs.description:
Tabs for switching a view in place or between pages. Across (the default) they are underline
tabs: a row over a bottom rule, the current tab underlined in the accent. `orientation="vertical"`
is the pill rail instead, the current tab filled, for a `SidebarLayout` aside, and takes a
`size`. `items` are `{ value, label }` buttons (`value` and `onChange` are the caller's state;
the arrow keys, Home and End move between tabs) or links (`href`, an in-app one through
`LinkProvider`; `selected` on an item, or `value`, marks the current one, which gets
`aria-current`). An item may carry a `count`, and a button one `disabledReason` (it stays
reachable by the arrows and its reason is a tooltip) or a bare `disabled`; `disabled` on the row disables every tab. `label` names the tab list. The panel is
the caller's: give it `role="tabpanel"`, and a tab `controls` to point at it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Every option is disabled, e.g. until the page has hydrated.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: items
props.description: The options in order: `{ value, label }` buttons, or links (`href`), the current link marked by its `selected` or by a `value` equal to the group's. Either may carry a `count`; a button may be `disabled`.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name of the group.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the option's `value` when one is chosen, by click or arrow key.

props.name: orientation
props.description:
`horizontal` is a row of underline tabs over a bottom rule; `vertical` is the pill rail, a
column at the rail's width for a `SidebarLayout` aside, where the up and down arrows move
between button tabs.

props.name: size
props.description: The pills' height and text, on the scale of a `Button`. Only the vertical rail takes a `size`.

props.name: value
props.description: The `value` of the current option; for links, an alternative to `selected` on the item.

Text.name: Text
Text.description:
Running text. A paragraph (`p`; `as="span"` for a run inside a row, a cell or a sentence),
text-base/6 normal, secondary (text-sm/5 under an `AppShell density="compact"`, text-base/7 inside
a `Prose`). A block of it
stops at a readable line length (`max-w-[72ch]`), wherever it sits. `strong` emphasises it:
font-medium in the primary ink, unless `tone` says otherwise.
`preserveNewlines` keeps the line breaks in the text (a user-typed note); runs of spaces still collapse.
`tone` colours it by meaning (`positive` for "Saved.", `danger` for an error, `muted` for a quieter line),
`numeric` sets tabular figures, `mono` the monospace face, and `lines` shows at most 1 to 4 lines,
ending in an ellipsis (the full text becomes its `title`). `align` sets it at `start`, `center` or `end`.
`italic` slants it, `breakWords` breaks a long unbroken string at the edge of its box, and `minWidth="amount"`
fixes a width and right-aligns the figure in it (a column of amounts lines up); it does not take `align`.

props.name: align
props.description:
Set the text at `start`, `center` or `end` of its block. The run becomes block-level, so the
alignment has a box to act on (a table header cell, a right-hand column).

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render (each role has a semantic default); the other props follow it.

props.name: breakWords
props.description: Break a long unbroken string (a URL, a token) where the container ends, instead of overflowing.

props.name: italic
props.description: Italic: a muted hint or a caption.

props.name: lines
props.description:
Show at most this many lines (1 to 4) and end in an ellipsis: `1` cuts the run where its
container ends, `2` to `4` wrap and stop. With plain-text content the full text becomes the
`title`. A "Show all" toggle is the app's own state: `lines={open ? undefined : 3}`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: minWidth
props.description: A fixed width: `amount` is a right-aligned money figure, min-w-24, in tabular figures.

props.name: mono
props.description: The monospace face, for an id, a path or a command.

props.name: numeric
props.description: Tabular figures, so a column of amounts lines up.

props.name: preserveNewlines
props.description: Keep the line breaks in the text (a user-typed note); runs of spaces still collapse.

props.name: strong
props.description: Emphasis: font-medium in the primary ink (`tone` still wins).

props.name: tone
props.description:
The ink: `neutral`, the default, is the role's own; `muted` and `accent` set the hierarchy of
the text; `positive`, `warn`, `danger` and `info` say what a run means (see `TextTone`).

Textarea.name: Textarea
Textarea.description: A multi-line text input, styled like `Input`. `rows` defaults to 3. Takes `size`, `width` and `mono` too. The `ref` reaches the `<textarea>`, for focus control.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the field; say why in its `Field` hint.

props.name: mono
props.description: The monospace face, for pasted CSV or statement text, where the columns must line up. Off by default.

props.name: name
props.description: The key the value posts under in a form.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: A hint shown while the field is empty; never the label.

props.name: ref
props.description: The `<textarea>` itself, for focus control.

props.name: rows
props.description: How many lines tall it starts.

props.name: size
width
props.description: `full` (default) fills the parent; `fill` grows to fill the room left in a row beside other items (it can shrink to nothing, so buttons stay on the line); `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg` are fixed; `auto` adds no width class, so the control is as wide as the browser makes it.

TextLink.name: TextLink
TextLink.description:
An inline text link in the accent colour. Every anchor prop goes on the `<a>`; an in-app `href`
is drawn by the app's router link through `LinkProvider`.
`size` pins the type size (`sm`, `md` or `lg`), `tone` gives it a meaning's colour and `mono` sets the
monospace face.

props.name: external
props.description: Opens in a new tab: adds `target="_blank"` and `rel="noreferrer"`.

props.name: href
props.description: Where the link goes; an in-app path goes through the app's `LinkProvider`.

props.name: mono
props.description: The monospace face, for a path, an id or a command.

props.name: size
props.description:
The link's own type size: `sm` is `text-xs`, `md` `text-sm` and `lg` `text-base`. Left out, it
takes the size of the text around it: a link inside prose has no default size.

props.name: stretch
props.description: The link covers its nearest `relative` ancestor, so the whole row or card is the click target.

props.name: tone
props.description:
A meaning's colour, as on the inline roles: `warn` for a warning link, `danger`, `positive`,
`info` or `muted`. Left out, the link is the accent colour.

props.name: underline
props.description: Always underlined, for a link set inside running text, where colour alone does not mark it (WCAG 1.4.1).

Timeline.name: Timeline
Timeline.description:
A vertical list of events, newest or oldest first as the caller orders them. A named `<ol>` of
`TimelineItem`s on a rail; with no children it draws `empty` (an `EmptyState`, one muted line here)
instead of an empty list. While `loading` with no items it draws three items of bones, never
`empty`.

props.name: empty
props.description: Drawn in place of the list when there are no items: an `EmptyState`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the list (`aria-label`), e.g. "Status history".

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

TimelineItem.name: TimelineItem
TimelineItem.description:
One event: a `title` (a `Pill`, a heading), a `time` the app has already formatted, and the
`children` as a note under them. `tone` colours the marker dot with the Callout's set. While
`loading` an empty `title` is a bone.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: time
props.description: When, already formatted by the app, small and muted beside the title.

props.name: title
props.description: What happened: text, a `Pill` or a heading.

props.name: tone
props.description: The marker dot's colour. Defaults to `neutral`, a plain ring. Say it in the text too: colour alone says nothing to a screen reader.

ToastRegion.name: ToastRegion
ToastRegion.description:
The page's toasts: short notices fixed to the bottom of the viewport, from a list the app holds.
Mount it once, at the root beside `AppShell`; add a toast to `toasts` to show it, and drop it in
`onDismiss` to remove it. A `neutral`, `info` or `positive` toast with no `actions` leaves on its
own after five seconds (paused while the pointer is over it or focus is in it); a `warn` or
`danger` toast, or one with `actions`, stays until dismissed. The region is a named landmark with
a polite `role="status"`, kept in the page while empty, so each new toast is read once. A toast
raised while a `Dialog` or `Drawer` is open sits under it until it closes.

props.name: dismissLabel
props.description: The close button's name.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The region's accessible name.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Called by a toast's close button and when a self-hiding toast's time is up: drop it from `toasts`.

props.name: toasts
props.description: What is shown, oldest first. `[]` shows nothing and keeps the live region in the page.

toISODate.name: toISODate
toISODate.description: `"1990-05-17"` for `CalendarDate(1990, 5, 17)`; `""` for no date, so it drops into a form field.

TrendChart.name: TrendChart
TrendChart.description:
A chart of one or two series over ordered buckets (weeks, months), as bars or a line, on a
y-axis from 0. The y-axis is labelled 0, half and a rounded maximum; the x-axis names the
buckets. A screen reader gets the same figures as a table. While `loading` the frame, the bucket
names and the key stay drawn and the plot is one bone, since 0 is a real value.

props.name: buckets
props.description: The x-axis labels, in order (`"W12"`, `"Mar"`).

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: kind
props.description: `bar` for a count in each bucket, `line` for a level over time.

props.name: label
props.description: What the chart shows: its accessible name and the caption of its table.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: series
props.description:
One or two series, each `{ label, tone, values }`. A `null` value, or a `values` list shorter
than `buckets`, is missing. Two series draw a Legend under the chart.

Video.name: Video
Video.description:
A `<video>` with controls, full width and rounded; it loads metadata only, so the page does not
pull the file until it is played. `src` is the app's own video; `captions` is a WebVTT file,
offered as the default track. `children` is the fallback for a browser that cannot play it.

props.name: captions
props.description: A WebVTT file, offered as the default captions track.

props.name: poster
props.description: The image shown before play; use a local one.

props.name: src
props.description: The video file, the app's own.
